Last Friday (21st) was the sentencing of the Hong Kong Alliance case. In the early morning, police escorted a woman who was queuing for a seat in the public gallery into a police vehicle. In response to enquiries, the police said the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty", and "seditious intent".

At around 5 a.m. last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During this time, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue "was suspected of having a shirt with a bit of seditious intent", and took her away in a police vehicle. While officers were removing the woman, several officers kept directing reporters to leave, saying "take you to the press area", and pulled the orange cordon line towards near Ying Wa Street. Once the woman had boarded the police vehicle, they put away the cordon line. On that day, a "court-watcher" who was queued near the woman pointed out that she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

The Collective (集誌社) enquired with the police about the reason the woman was taken away and whether she had been arrested. The police replied this morning (the 24th) that during a security operation conducted around the West Kowloon Courts on 21 August, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty", and "seditious intent", and was detained for investigation.
